name: orbkin-sprite-creature

iterations.log: Fresh Opus agent, skill v1 (commit 611df8f), scratch copy of game/, ~34 min, 87 tool calls, ~$2.3 of judge votes. Added kin19 'Stiltfern' (Flora/Terra rare single): a root-knot body on four arched root stilts with a moss saddle, a fern crozier and cyan crystal toes. S0 baseline (cast facts, lineup, Cragmaul battle). S1/S2 brief with a 3-concept table (stilt walker 22, loam mole 16, furrow worm 14; 'leaf + rock' excluded). S3 blockout: lineup max IoU 0.386. S4 three rounds: round 1 sandstone body blended into the meadow's sand floor (the brief had assumed grass); round 2 pale lichen body; round 3 dark bark legs, bigger body, eyes 4.14x5.47 texels, 1,366 tris, 1 draw call, grounded, 4 colour blocks, lineup max IoU 0.487 vs Cragmaul, solidity 0.576 < median 0.626. S5: pasted the keyed playKeys code, wrote LUNGE_KEYS (rear-and-stamp, 48 f, wind-up 14% H, stretch 36% H) and HIT_KEYS (22 f), a tick-aligned discrete blink (30/30 closed); strip lint clean (anticipation 13 f, back 5.0 texels, stretch 1.36, squash 0.66, overshoot 2.3 texels). S6: ip lineup PASS (max 4), ip battle crop PASS (max 3); strip judge better 3/3 both orders ($0.37); pairwise vs Cragmaul: round 2 worse on desk and phone full ('pale spindly sprite washes out against the sand', 'faceless'), round 3 no_difference on desk (full 1/2 + 0/2, crop 2/2 + 1/2) and phone (2/2 + 0/2), canaries passed. S7: typecheck clean, 280/280 tests, eslint clean on the changed files; no engine files touched.
skillProblems: facts.ts imported the real repo's game by a relative path, so lineup.py/read_sheet.py ignored --game and measured the wrong checkout (the pilot copied the scripts into its workspace to work around it)
SKILL.md named the S0 baseline capture battle-cragmaul-*.png while read_sheet wrote battle-kin-*.png

keys_lint --ts could not parse a plain array literal (bracket matching only handled braces) and exited 1 instead of 2; its default units (body-height fractions) disagreed with playKeys (model units), overstating travel 1.6-1.8x
motion.md's playKeys showed each cel one frame longer than its table and in-betweened the impact key, so the contact pose landed ~6 frames late; the pilot had to patch it
strips.py linted the hit strip with attack rules (NO_ANTICIPATION etc.) so 'lint flags empty' was impossible for a hit; FLOATY_STRIKE counted the held wind-up as strike time
strips.sh had no way to capture the motion=tween baseline strip; the pilot drove capture.mjs by hand
read_sheet reused a stale dist after design edits (no rebuild), and the eye-size hint ignored yaw foreshortening

judge.py: one timed-out vote crashed the run and lost the paid votes; a 'could not be loaded' canary vote still counted; nothing warned against running gates in parallel; strong position bias hid behind no_difference
report.py only looked in the top of --dir, so sheet/lineup results in s3/ and s4/ were listed as NOT RUN
design.md never stated the meadow battle floor is a light warm sand path, so round 1 was spent on sand-on-sand
the brief paragraph already contained the winning concept before the divergence table; the three concepts were scored by guess without blockouts

no check caught that the stilt body plan reads as a spider and that a 4x5-texel single-tone eye still fuses with dark knuckles into a faceless mass in the bake; the blink rule had no code; the ip check on the full lineup sheet carried the cast's known flags; the hit's per-cel blink-hide blanked the sprite 6-7 frames at a time

judge.vsCurrent: On par to slightly below the current cast as still art and clearly above it in motion. The silhouette is genuinely more distinct than any existing kin (worst IoU 0.487, solidity below the median) and the keyed lunge beat the shipped tween 6/6, but in the actual battle frame kin19 reads as a brown-legged spider with a white cap and a black faceless mass, which is a weaker read than Cragmaul's golem-with-a-face at desk size and only equal on phone; the pairwise gate agreed (no_difference on desk full, crop and phone, with the judge repeatedly saying 'dark blob', 'weak/unreadable face').
strengths: Silhouette is the most distinct in the cast: high gapped stilts and the side-view crozier read as a '?' hook at 32 px; measured, not asserted (IoU 0.487 worst vs Cragmaul, solidity 0.576 < 0.626 median).

Keyed attack is a real step over the current tween: visible rear-back anticipation held 4 f, one stretched smear cel, contact squash, hop past rest, settle; strip lint clean and the blind strip gate was better 3/3 in both orders ($0.37).
Blink problem actually fixed and measured (30/30 closed at the 10 fps bake) instead of claimed.

Honest, script-backed process: frozen-clock captures, canary passed, both orders, costs quoted, 'still weak' and 'inferred, not measured' sections name the real problems (face lost, spider drift, position-biased phone verdict, hit lint misapplied).
Builder craft within the kit is competent: 1366 tris, tapered tubes with knuckle orbs and crystal toes, nod rig on the crozier, one mesh, grounded; species/routes/test entries all pass.
IP is clean by construction (max 4, 'generic') and the name passes the banned regex; the forbidden-shape list in the brief shows the agent knew the Bulbasaur/Torterra traps.
weaknesses: Face is lost in the battle bake: the eyes are two pure-dark discs (4x5.5 texels, ~a third of the head) with the dark knuckle orbs sitting at eye height on both sides, so at 34 texels the whole front of the body fuses into one black mass under a white cap. The eye-size floor was met while the face still vanished; the check measures pupil size in model space, not eye contrast in the baked sprite.

Element read fails at sprite size: Flora shows only as a green sprout, Terra not at all (cyan toes are 2 px, the moss saddle is hidden under the crozier from the battle yaw, the pink bud is invisible). The judge's reads were 'spider', 'Joltik/Tarountula/Paras with a sprout', never 'plant' or 'rock'.

The signature part only exists in the side view: from the 3/4 front the battle camera actually uses, the forward-curling crozier collapses to a vertical stalk with two leaves (a generic 'sprout on head'). The lineup passed because it scores three views equally.

Body-plan drift to arachnid: four long splayed arched legs around a round body reads as a spider regardless of leg count; the IP judge named five spider Pokemon across both views and the pilot noted it, but 'generic / PASS' hid a design-level archetype problem that contradicts the Flora/Terra brief.

Colour blocking reads as white / black / brown / green sliver, not the briefed 60/30/10 lichen-moss-accent; read_sheet counted 4 blocks on the model, not on the bake, so the check passed while the sprite lost two of them. The body is an untextured sphere with no markings, far from the bar's 'designed' read.

Divergence was partly theatre: the S1 brief paragraph already contained the winning concept, name, signature and attack before the S2 table; concepts B and C are one-liners scored by guess (no blockouts, no lineup numbers).

The promised behaviour ('rears back, stamps with front stilts, legs splay on hit') is not what plays: ActKey can only squash/lean/translate the whole body, so the rear-up is a rigid billboard tilt around the body centre and the legs never articulate.

Hit reads as the creature vanishing, not being hurt: the recoil cel is a full-white silhouette (pose unreadable), then the blink-hide is applied per cel, which with 6-7 frame cels hides the sprite for 6-7 real frames at a time (hidden ~10 of 18 frames). strips.py linted the hit with attack rules so the real defect was not flagged.
The S0 baseline capture was in hand yet the R1 brief assumed a green floor; a round was spent on sand-on-sand before the agent looked at the floor.

Gate verdicts are position-biased no_difference with only 2 votes per order (phone: 2/2 first, 0/2 second), and the skill lets the loop stop at no_difference, so a kin that does not beat the slot occupant shipped as done.
A global change to CreatureView.update (discrete blink for all 18 kin) and to lunge/hit playback was made with no regression gate on any existing kin.
skillFixes: Split S1/S2 so the brief cannot prime the pick: S1 lists only constraints (element pair, stage/texels, arena floor hex+value from read_sheet, budgets); S2 writes three concepts with identical fields each (body plan, signature part, behaviour, palette roles, forbidden shape, 32 px thumbnail); the working name, signature and behaviour move into S1b AFTER the table. Make report.py reject a brief.md whose paragraph precedes the divergence table.

Make divergence measured: require a 2-4 primitive blockout per concept and `lineup.py --concept a|b|c` on all three (cheap), and have the table's 'silhouette distinctness' and 'solidity' columns be the printed numbers, not 1-5 guesses.

Replace the model-space pupil check with a baked-sprite face check in read_sheet.py at the battle yaw: (a) eye-box mean value differs >= 25% from the 2-texel ring around it, (b) no non-eye block within 15% value of the eye colour touches that ring (knuckles, legs, nose), (c) eye area <= 20% of the head's frontal area, (d) eyes on a dark or dark-adjacent head must be two-tone (sclera or iris) because a 1-tone dark disc fuses with any dark neighbour. Add to design.md §faces: 'nothing dark at eye height beside the head; joints, knuckles and paws sit below the chin line'.

Add a blind read test (`judge.py read <battle crop>`, 3 runs): 'name the animal or thing, its element(s), and point to the face'. Gate: element pair named in >= 2/3, face located in 3/3, and any off-element archetype (spider/insect for a non-bug element, 'sprout on a critter', 'rock with arms') is a FAIL that re-plans from S2. The ip check's 'generic' PASS must not be the only archetype signal.

Add to design.md §silhouette an archetype-trap list: four or more long splayed arched legs round a ball body = arachnid; a stalk with leaves on the head = Oddish/Pikmin/Paras sprout; a bulb on the back = Bulbasaur; and require every leg plan to break the trap (two long + two stubby, knee direction, feet shapes).

Score the signature part at the battle view: lineup.py renders the foe yaw used by hd2dBattle (and the player-side yaw) and prints the signature part's share of the silhouette and its bounding-box distinctness at that yaw; the skill requires >= 8% of sprite area and a non-generic outline in the battle view, not only in the side view.

Count colour blocks and element hues on the baked battle crop, not on the model: read_sheet reports the share of each palette entry inside the foe box at desk and phone; the skill requires each element's hue family to own >= 15% of the sprite and the briefed 60/30/10 roles to survive within +-10 points; otherwise S4 fails. Add a §markings rule: at least one 2-texel-wide marking (mask, saddle band, belly patch) in a value distinct from both neighbours, visible at the battle yaw, so the body is not a plain sphere.

S0 must print the floor fact: read_sheet samples the median colour and value under the foe's feet in the baseline capture and writes it to facts.json; design.md carries a table of every arena's floor hex/value; the S1 brief's 'arena floor' field must quote that number (report.py checks it).

Constrain or extend motion to what the rig can play: motion.md must state that ActKey moves the whole body only, so behaviour briefs may only promise sq/lean/fwd/up acting; or add a `rig` field to ActKey ({ kind, amp }) that drives the existing rig kinds (wag/nod/flap/twitch) per key so stilts, tails and ears can splay and stamp. Also pivot lean at the ground contact for standing kin and add a strips.py check that the feet never leave the contact shadow during wind-up (a rigid card tilt around the centre was visible in the strip).

Fix the hit recipe and its lint: in motion.md's verified code compute blink-hide per 2 frames inside a per-frame loop (never per cel: cels are 5-7 frames long), cap hidden frames at <= 1/3 of the recovery with max 2 consecutive, flash as emissive 0.6-0.7 on the recoil cel (a full-white fill hides the pose) or flash 1 cel then show the recoil pose un-flashed for >= 3 f. Give strips.py a `--kind hit` rule set (recoil texels >= 2, flash <= 3 f, visible fraction, pose readable) so a hit is never linted with NO_ANTICIPATION/NO_STRETCH.

Tighten the gate: judge.py pair runs >= 3 votes per order, reports a position-bias flag when one order wins all its votes, and tags each reason with keywords (face, blob, blends, outline, texture); SKILL.md's done criterion for a NEW kin becomes crop `better` and full `no_difference` or better versus the slot occupant, and a no_difference after 2 rounds re-plans from S2 instead of stopping. The next round must target the most frequent reason tag.

Scope rule for shared code: any edit to CreatureView (blink, playKeys) or the bake must be gated on one existing kin (Ashkit or Cragmaul, same frozen capture before/after, `no_difference` or `better`) before the new kin is judged, or be opt-in per Design (`blink: 'tick'`). Add that gate to S7 and list it in the report skeleton.

Add an in-game texel proxy comparison to S4: read_sheet places the new kin's battle crop beside the two best-reading cast faces (Ashkit, Cragmaul) at the same scale in one image and the agent must state which parts of the face/signature are lost before S5; the pilot had proxy-kin19.png showing the knee orbs fusing with the eyes and did not act on it.

iterations.log: Fresh Opus agent, skill v2 (commit e545d42), fresh scratch copy of game/, ~42 min, 101 tool calls, ~$2.2 of judge votes (+$0.4 for the strip judge run by the author after repairing it). Added kin19 'Delvebill' (Flora/Terra rare single): a long-billed ground bird with a cocked head, light saddle, bloom bib, shag tufts and cyan crystal shards. S0: floor under the foe measured (#fcd18d / 213 desk, #fce1a8 / 226 phone), cast solidity median 0.6295. S1: constraints-only brief. S2: three blockouts measured with lineup.py (isopod 0.62 IoU / 0.82 solidity, mole 0.69 / 0.88, ground bird 0.74 / 0.59); picked the bird (the two losers were flagged blobs). S3: blockout clean (0.77 / 0.55); species, LINES/DESIGNS, a meadow wild slot, cap test 19. S4: three face rounds (bill shrank to a stick in the near-head-on foe bake; eye box sat on the bill; iris made the pupil < 3x3) then a re-plan with the head cocked 0.75 rad and crystal shards: lineup 0.572 / 0.603, eyes 7.1x4.8 texels, 1,310 tris, 1 draw call, grounded; blind read PASS (Flora 3/3, Terra 3/3, face 3/3). S5: keyed playKeys pasted, KIN19_LUNGE_KEYS (51 f, wind-up 18% H, stretch 1.38), KIN19_HIT_KEYS (22 f), discrete blink 97.5% closed; strips: keyed back 5.1 texels / overshoot 2.3 vs tween back 2.8 / none, hit recoil 3.7 texels, no lint flags; judge.py strip crashed (NameError from a bad text replacement) so no strip verdict in the pilot; run after the repair: no_difference with position bias (candidate 1/3 shown first, 3/3 shown second). S6: ip PASS (max 4) on lineup column and crop; desk gate: crop better 3/3 + 3/3, full no_difference (2/3 + 0/3), canary passed; phone gate no_difference (2/3 + 0/3), reasons 'smaller, spindly, flat, less grounded'; a chunkier round 2 regressed the read and stayed no_difference (3/3 + 1/3), reverted. S7: Cragmaul re-capture pixel-identical to S0, typecheck clean, 280/280 tests, eslint clean on src/tests; the final frame after the shared blink edit landed on a closed-eye blink: final read FAIL (face 1/3), final desk full worse (crop still better 3/3 + 3/3). No engine files touched.
skillProblems: judge.py strip crashed with NameError STRIP_PROMPT: a text replacement in the revision had matched 'IP_PROMPT = (' inside 'STRIP_PROMPT = (' and renamed it; the fallback skill orbkin-visual-gate does not exist on the branch

the discrete blink edit (required in S5) plus a frozen clock can put the gate frame on a closed-eye blink; the workflow captured and gated in S4 and changed the blink in S5 with no re-capture, and S7 only checked Cragmaul
read_sheet's near-eye box measured the sclera (pupilTone 211) and once sat on the bill covering the eye while reporting contrast 0.72; it never checked for a dark pupil
design.md said the foe shows its 3/4 face; the foe actually faces nearly head-on, so a forward bill became a stub; FLAT_POSES.turn applies to your own kin only
the battle's size formula (max(h, 0.8*max(x,z)) with a ^0.4 softening) was undocumented, shrinking a long kin next to Cragmaul ('small, spindly')
lineup.py counted concept blockouts in the cast median and its 64-px tiles clipped wide silhouettes
motion.md's sample QUAD_HIT tail failed keys_lint's own sub-texel rule and its head block duplicated the existing spring helper
the iris option and 'an eye no taller than a third of the head' cannot both give a 3x3 pupil; only the sclera works and it was not stated
read_sheet exited 1 on a BLOCKS flag that 11 of 18 cast kin also carry and SKILL.md's exit-0 list did not mention
stated numbers drifted from measurements (floor #fde1a9/226 vs #fcd18d/213 under Cragmaul; Cragmaul contrast '0.01' vs 0.32 measured; blink '100%' vs 97.5%)
report.py picked the newest sheet.json (a Cragmaul re-capture) and reported the kin as NOT RUN; it also listed verdict copies by bare file name
full-frame pair verdicts followed display position (2/3 first vs 0/3 second three times) and were labelled no_difference without a bias flag
strips.sh had no 8-frame strip and the task's LUNGE_KEYS name did not match the per-archetype table names; strips.py's lint JSON overwrote the capture JSON
the blind read passed on element names and a found face while every vote saw a bush-on-legs holding a claw: the body plan and signature were never checked

the colour advice 'dark olive mass + light moss top' was the skill's own untested default and the green melted into the foliage band behind the foe; only the floor was measured, not the backdrop at head height

judge.vsCurrent: On par at best, and worse where it matters. In the 2x crop kin19 beats the game's weakest reader (Cragmaul) on outline, colour pop and face contrast, and its keyed lunge is visibly better than the shipped tween; but in the full frame on desk and phone it is no better than the current cast (judges: small, spindly, green melts into the foliage band, less grounded), the shipped frame has its eyes shut and fails the read gate, and the designed concept (a long-billed ground bird probing with a crystal drill) never reaches the player: all 15 blind-read votes saw a bush/bulb/blob on legs with a wide pink mouth holding a pale blue claw, which is the same blob-with-a-face class as Mossling and Verdantusk.
strengths: The S1 brief is genuinely constraints-only and the S2 table carries measured worst-IoU and solidity per concept, with the pick and the losers' reasons written down; the final S3 lineup is clean (worst IoU 0.572, solidity 0.603 under the 0.626 median).

In model space the concept is original and appealing: kiwi-like prober, sandstone bill with a cyan crystal drill tip, bloom bib, two-size shag tufts and two-size shards, a cocked listening head; no franchise icon is near it (ip max 4, generic).
The baked crop has a clean dark outline, 3-tone ramped greens, a strong pink and cyan accent and real floor separation; the crop gate won 6/6 in both orders twice against the baseline.

The keyed attack strip shows a real crouch-back wind-up (6 texels), a 5-frame hold, one stretched strike cel, a wide contact squash, a hop back past rest and a landing squash: anticipation, impact and follow-through all exist, and the hit strip has a single strong recoil cel, a 2-frame blink-hide and a 22-frame settle; keys_lint, hit lint, strip lint and blink_check (97.5% closed) are all clean.

The report is honest: it never claims a verdict the JSON lacks, records the strip judge crash, the final-frame FAIL, the reverted scale round, the BLOCKS flag and the shared-code regression check (S0 recapture pixel-identical).
weaknesses: The signature and body plan are lost at sprite size: the bill lies along the body as a thin brown stripe, the crystal tip sits at foot level and reads as a held tool/claw, the bloom bib under the eyes reads as a wide pink mouth, and head and body are the same green so the cocked head is invisible; nobody read bird, bill or probe. The read gate still said PASS because it only checks element names and face-found.

The main colour was chosen by the skill's own untested rule (dark olive mass + light moss top) and then judged muddy and blending into the foliage band behind the foe in 20+ votes; the skill measured only the floor, not the backdrop at head height.

The final shipped captures were frozen mid-blink after the shared blink edit: eyes shut, final read 1/3 face, final desk full frame worse. The kin was shipped on gates that pass only on a superseded frame, and ip was not re-run on the final frame.
Full-frame pair verdicts are position-biased noise (candidate wins 2/3 shown first vs 0/3 shown second, three times; 3/3 vs 1/3 once) and the JSON labels that no_difference with no bias flag.

The divergence was a one-horse race: concepts A and B were a lumpy ball and a ball with triangles (solidity 0.82 and 0.88, both flagged blobs), so the table could only pick C; the chosen blockout then grew a head, bib and shards that were never silhouette-tested as a concept.
read_sheet's face numbers measure the whole eye (7x4.8 texels, pupilTone 211 = the sclera), not the dark pupil; the pupil >= 3x3 rule was satisfied by a white sclera box.
Legs are 2-3 texels wide, which is 1-2 px on phone; judges called it spindly and flat and said it floats. BLOCKS 8 (aim 3-5) was dismissed as not a pilot criterion.

The attack table is QUAD_ATTACK with the lean bumped; the stretch is vertical, so the stab reads as the whole card standing up tall rather than a forward thrust, and the hit's recoil cel is a full-white silhouette for about 6 frames rather than the 0.7 flash the reference promises. The strip judge crashed (NameError STRIP_PROMPT) so the motion was never gated.

The baseline is the cast's worst reader (Cragmaul, face contrast 0.01); 'better than Cragmaul in the crop' is a low bar and says nothing about how kin19 sits next to Ashkit in the same frame, where it loses clearly.
The bake is noisy inside the silhouette (shag blades and facets become speckle on the saddle), still a baked model rather than the hand-placed 3-4 tone pixel shading of the bar.
skillFixes: judge.py read: PASS must also require the intended body plan and signature. Add --plan <class> --signature <part>; PASS needs the archetype to be in that class in >= 2/3 votes and the signature vote to name the intended part; make 'blob/bush/ball/bulb/melon on legs' and any 'holding an object' reading an automatic FAIL regardless of element. Put the same rule in SKILL.md rule 2 and the S4 checklist: a face found on a blob is not a pass.

Stills must never be captured mid-blink. capture.mjs and read_sheet.py --battle add &blink=0 (CreatureView honours it) or pick the frozen t outside every blink tick; read_sheet flags EYES_SHUT when no dark pupil tone exists inside the eye box; SKILL.md S7: any shared-code edit (blink, playKeys) after a passing gate invalidates that gate, re-run read, ip and pair on the final frame, and Done requires the FINAL frame's JSON to pass.

read_sheet.py: measure the dark pupil separately from the sclera (pupil box >= 3x3 texels, pupilTone < ringMedian) and print both; design.md §faces: the pupil rule is about the dark part, the sclera is the contrast carrier.

Replace the untested colour advice in design.md §colour ('dark bark/olive mass + light moss top') with a measurement: read_sheet.py --battle also prints the backdrop ring behind the sprite (median colour of a 4-texel ring, upper and lower halves) and flags BACKDROP when the main block is within 20% value and 60 degrees hue of the ring behind the head; the brief must carry floor AND backdrop numbers. Standing rule 7 was violated by the skill's own text.

Signature protrusion gate: tag the signature part in the builder (k.tag('signature', () => ...)); lineup.py renders the battle yaw (the foe's bake view) with and without the tag and prints the protruding area in texels outside the body hull; S3 exit requires >= 3 texels of protrusion at the battle yaw and the lineup column marks the head end (dot at the eye position) so silhouettes are judged with a known facing (the ip judge read the bill as a tail).

design.md §faces and §colour: the head must separate from the body either in silhouette at the battle yaw (neck gap, crest, bill beyond the hull) or by its own colour block (a mask lighter than the body by >= 20% value); forbid any wide saturated marking at mouth height under the eyes unless it is the mouth (the bib became a mouth), and require the blind read to name every accent block as the intended part.

§divergence: a table is valid only when all three blockouts pass the solidity rule (below the cast median) and worst IoU <= 0.8; a flagged blockout must be re-blocked before the pick, so the table compares three eligible concepts rather than one survivor and two strawmen. Then the picked blockout must be re-run through lineup.py after secondary forms are added (S4), not only at S3.

§proportions: ground kin legs >= 3 texels wide at their stage's texel height (print per-limb width in read_sheet from the leg() radii x texelsPerUnit) and a contact-shadow darkness check under the feet vs the cast median; 'spindly, floats, less grounded' were the top full-frame reasons.
Make BLOCKS a gate, not advice: read_sheet exit 1 on > 5 blocks blocks S4, and SKILL.md states that no script flag may be waved off as 'not a criterion' without an owner check.

judge.py pair: emit the position-bias flag in the JSON and return 'inconclusive' (not no_difference) when the two orders disagree by >= 2 votes; for the full frame use a composite with randomised left/right sides or gate on the crop plus a measured size/limb check; add a second baseline that is the cast's best meadow reader (Ashkit or Breezel as foe) so 'better than Cragmaul' is not the only bar.

motion.md: add a biped/bird stab-peck table (lean-dominant, stretch along travel, short hold, head-led) and a stretchAxis: 'travel' option in playKeys; require the design's table to differ from the template archetype in the beat that carries the promised behaviour (keys_lint diff vs the template); lint the recoil cel's mean luminance so the flash matches the stated 0.7/0.85.

Fix judge.py strip (NameError STRIP_PROMPT), add judge.py selftest that imports every subcommand's prompt and runs a dry vote, and make the strip verdict a hard S5 gate: no keyed table ships without a judged strip.

report.py: the skeleton must gate on the final frame's JSON set (read, ip, pair desk, pair phone, strip) and print NOT DONE with the failing gates listed, so a report cannot present round-1 passes as the shipped state.

note: Both pilots scored 5/10 (on par with the current cast as still art, better in motion). After pilot 2 the author fixed, in the delivered skill: the strip judge crash, blink-free gate stills, the dark-pupil measurement, body-plan and signature checks in the blind read (pilot 2's kin now FAILs it, as the judge read it), the position-bias flag, a final-gate block in the report, the foe-facing and size-formula facts, and the sample tables; the backdrop measurement, signature protrusion gate, limb-width check, stab-peck table and the second baseline are not implemented.
